tEn: Danny Martinez: Thriving in Today's Design Job Market
tZh: Danny Martinez：在当今设计就业市场中脱颖而出
sEn: Danny Martinez, CEO of Decimals, breaks down how the design job market is shifting and what designers and hiring managers need to know.
sZh: Decimals 首席执行官 Danny Martinez 解析设计就业市场的变革，以及设计师和招聘经理需要了解的关键趋势。

consensus.en: Design roles are blurring; one person now covers design, engineering, and product.
consensus.zh: 设计角色正在模糊化；一个人现在要覆盖设计、工程和产品。

consensus.en: Hiring managers prioritize tinkerers who build with latest tools over pedigree.
consensus.zh: 招聘经理更看重使用最新工具动手的创客，而非背景出身。

consensus.en: Portfolios should show proof of human: unique, crafted, and personal.
consensus.zh: 作品集应展示‘人类证明’：独特、精心打磨且个人化。

consensus.en: Writing and systems thinking are green flags for designers today.
consensus.zh: 写作和系统思维是当今设计师的绿色信号。

consensus.en: In-demand designers have leverage; companies must compete for them.
consensus.zh: 抢手的设计师拥有议价权；公司必须竞争才能得到他们。

consensus.en: Compensation for top design engineers can reach $300k or more.
consensus.zh: 顶级设计工程师的薪酬可达30万美元或更高。

contrarian.en: Big company logos like FAANG are now red flags, not credentials.
contrarian.zh: FAANG等大公司背景现在反而是红色信号，而非资历。

contrarian.en: Job titles like design engineer are meaningless; skills matter more.
contrarian.zh: 设计工程师等职位头衔毫无意义；技能更重要。

contrarian.en: Take-home assignments without discussion are rejected by top designers.
contrarian.zh: 没有讨论的带回家作业会被顶级设计师拒绝。

contrarian.en: Long interview processes are outdated; work trials are more effective.
contrarian.zh: 冗长的面试流程已过时；工作试用更有效。

contrarian.en: Vibe-coded portfolios are seen as thoughtless and boilerplate.
contrarian.zh: 氛围编码的作品集被视为缺乏思考且千篇一律。

contrarian.en: Freelance brand designers can earn $500k-$750k, rivaling full-time roles.
contrarian.zh: 自由品牌设计师年收入可达50-75万美元，媲美全职角色。

turns.en: Welcome to Dive Club. My name is Rid and this is where designers never stop learning. This week's episode is with Danny Martinez, who's the CEO of Decimals, which is the platform that I use to power pretty much everything that I'm doing with the Dive Talent Network. Needless to say, Danny has an incredible vantage point into the state of design hiring today. So, we're going to do a little deep dive into some of the key takeaways for both designers and hiring managers, and we even screen share a few examples of portfolios that are having success in the network today. So, let's start by jumping right into some of the key trends that Danny's noticing.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Dive Club。我是 Rid，这里是设计师永不停歇的学习之地。本周的嘉宾是 Danny Martinez，他是 Decimals 的 CEO，这个平台几乎支撑着我在 Dive Talent Network 里做的所有事情。不用说，Danny 对当今设计招聘的现状有着绝佳的观察视角。所以，我们将深入探讨一些对设计师和招聘经理都至关重要的要点，我们甚至会屏幕共享一些目前在网络中取得成功的作品集案例。那么，让我们直接切入 Danny 注意到的一些关键趋势吧。

turns.en: I feel like it's pretty fair to say that it kind of feels like the ground is just shifting underneath everyone's feet at the moment. It ends up resulting that you see pretty peculiar things coming out. People using all kinds of like new job titles to describe what they're looking for. People not really having a lot of clarity on like what does the ideal hire look like? I think that's one of the first things that comes to mind which is when we initially started talking to hiring managers and beginning at decimals it was very much about like hey talk to me about the ideal candidate you know give me the specifics talk to me about their profile and eventually I kind of came to the conclusion of like so much is changing and so much of what the hiring manager will tell you is different from what they're used to that they're kind of throwing out these oddball things of the like they must have exquisite taste and they must and you're just like okay cool that's that's great but I can't really use that for much and then you get into like okay cool let's let's get into the job titles and and even there you it can be somewhat helpful but it can also be something that leads you down the wrong path as well. So like I think the one that is mostly talked about is design engineer. And whenever I get a new company, new hiring manager telling me they want a design engineer, I'm just like okay, let's pause without using the word design engineer. Tell me what you're looking for. The thing that comes back is so different from hiring managers and hiring manager. The way I kind of simplified my mind is like do you want a designer that knows how to use Claude Code because there's plenty of those or you want somebody who trained as an engineer, has background as an engineer that can design for themselves. Those are two very different profiles, but the same nomenclature gets used to like identify them. I think if there's like any theme that I can point to, it's just that there's so much that is changing right now that it is actually when you talk from person to person, they might think that they're hiring the same role. They might be using the same name to describe the role that actually ends up being super super different. I think the the general theme that comes back is I want someone that is a tinkerer, you know, is using the latest tools, is reimagining what it means to be a designer. We had a founder from a company. I won't reveal his name, but everybody will will know who he is. Pretty well-known company. And he kind of said to me, "Hey, I'm looking to hire a designer that doesn't really identify with just being a designer anymore. You know, they're creating prototypes. They are doing their own PRs. They are kind of rethinking what it means to do their role in the current landscape. And I think that's the thing that the more I speak to even designers. I spoke to guy called Oscar Lozano who has just landed at at Lovable recently and the way he described it to me is I guess the way I think about it where where is he's kind of just said hey if I look at my at the job that I do now versus what I used to do 18 months ago it's completely different game completely changed. The rules are not the same anymore. And these like silos that we relied on for years of engineering product design these are the handoff points like all of that it's like ripped that off. That's That's not going to get useful.
turns.zh: 我觉得可以说，眼下感觉就像大家脚下的地面在移动。结果就是你会看到一些很奇怪的现象。人们用各种新的职位头衔来描述他们想要找的人。人们其实并不太清楚理想的候选人到底应该是什么样。我首先想到的一点是，当我们最初开始和招聘经理交流、在 Decimals 起步的时候，我们问的是：跟我聊聊理想的候选人吧，给我具体信息，说说他们的背景。后来我逐渐得出结论：变化太大了，招聘经理告诉你的很多东西和他们过去习惯的完全不同，以至于他们会抛出一些古怪的要求，比如“他们必须有绝佳的品味”，你只能说好吧，这很棒，但我没法用这个来做什么。然后你深入到职位头衔，即使在那里，它可能有点帮助，但也可能把你引向错误的方向。所以，我觉得讨论最多的就是设计工程师。每当我遇到一个新公司、新的招聘经理告诉我他们想要一个设计工程师时，我就会说：好，我们先暂停一下，不要用“设计工程师”这个词。告诉我你到底想要什么。不同招聘经理给出的答案千差万别。我简化思考的方式是：你是想要一个会用 Claude Code 的设计师，因为这样的人很多；还是想要一个受过工程师训练、有工程师背景、能自己做设计的人？这是两种非常不同的画像，但人们却用同一个术语来指代他们。如果非要指出一个主题，那就是现在变化太多了，以至于当你和不同的人交谈时，他们可能以为自己在招聘同一个角色，可能用同一个名字来描述这个角色，但实际上却截然不同。普遍的主题是：我想要一个爱折腾的人，使用最新工具，重新定义设计师的含义。我们有一位公司的创始人，我不透露他的名字，但大家都会知道他是谁，是一家非常知名的公司。他对我说：“嘿，我想招聘一个不再仅仅认同自己是设计师的设计师。他们在创建原型，自己做 PR，他们在重新思考在当前环境下自己的角色意味着什么。”我觉得这就是我和设计师们交流越多越感受到的。我和一个叫 Oscar Lozano 的人聊过，他最近刚加入 Lovable，他描述的方式是：如果我看看我现在做的工作和 18 个月前做的相比，完全是不同的游戏，完全变了。规则不再一样了。我们多年来依赖的工程、产品设计这些孤岛，这些交接点，所有这些都被撕掉了。那不再有用了。

turns.zh: 先插播一条简短消息，然后我们继续。还记得 Jamie Ganon 来聊过用 AI 做创意总监吗？她参与了一个为 Claire Vo 的新公司做的精彩品牌项目。让我印象深刻的是，她如何用动效让整个揭幕过程栩栩如生。毫不意外，她用了 Jitter。一方面，它非常简单直观，即使你从未做过动效设计；另一方面，它又极其强大，你可以构建自己的创意工具来创建各种自定义动画和效果。多年来 Jitter 一直是我首选的动效工具，我强烈推荐。访问 dive.com/jitter 开始使用。我最喜欢的新兴工具之一叫 DESN，因为他们的新画布能为你提供整个产品在生产环境中的实时可视化地图。只需连接你的代码仓库，Destin 就会自动列出每个独特的屏幕和状态。这样你就能看到真正的源头，而不是过时的设计文件。然后你可以复制任何屏幕来并排探索想法，与团队分享，甚至可以通过 Destin 的 MCP 直接合并到生产环境。在我看来，这就是现代设计工作流的样子，你可以成为首批尝试的人之一。只需访问 dive.club.club/desen 与他们的联合创始人 Gab 预约聊天。别忘了告诉他们是我 Ridd 推荐的，这样你可以跳过排队。网址是 dive.comclub/desen dsn。现在，回到节目。

turns.en: I was thinking about this leading up to this call. I was like, if I was going to make a portfolio and try to get a role tomorrow, what label would I use? Because that Oscar code resonates so much. Like, my dayto-day is night and day than it was 18 months ago. Does that mean that this is just the new shape of designer? Do I need to reach for a different title? You know, and and I'm not really sure what to do with that. And I think it hits on this idea you're talking about with like the design engineer, which we see constantly. And I'm so glad you bring that up cuz I also I'm like, wait, what does that mean? What do you mean by that? Right? Because sometimes you'll read it and it's like, oh, this is basically a product designer job description. Straight up, it's a product designer. and then they're just playing with AI tools and then sometimes it's like no we want people to actually be able to come in and improve the quality and architecture of our front-end code.
turns.zh: 在这次通话之前我一直在想这个问题。我想，如果我要做一个作品集，明天试着找个工作，我该用什么标签？因为 Oscar 说的太有共鸣了。我的日常和 18 个月前相比简直是天壤之别。这是否意味着这就是设计师的新形态？我需要换一个不同的头衔吗？我真的不太确定该怎么处理。我觉得这正好触及了你说的设计工程师这个概念，我们经常看到。我很高兴你提到这个，因为我也在想，等等，那是什么意思？你指的是什么？对吧？因为有时候你读到它，会觉得，哦，这基本上就是产品设计师的职位描述。直说了，就是产品设计师，然后他们只是在玩 AI 工具。而有时候又像是，不，我们希望人们能真正进来改进我们前端代码的质量和架构。

turns.en: I think that's much more rare, but it totally exists, and they're using the same label, and that is a fundamentally different person in my mind.
turns.zh: 我觉得这种情况要少见得多，但它确实存在，而且他们用的是同一个头衔，但在我看来，这完全是两种不同的人。

turns.en: And a pretty interesting thing plays out. I think this is something that came up in the chat with Oscar, where he kind of rolled his eyes when we started talking about the design engineer thing. He was like, "Design engineer." I was like, "What's causing the eye roll? Tell me." And it's like, "Well, I just feel like a lot of people call themselves that when in reality they're not."
turns.zh: 然后出现了一个挺有意思的现象。我觉得这是和 Oscar 聊天时提到过的，当我们开始聊设计工程师这件事时，他有点翻白眼。他说：“设计工程师。”我说：“你为什么翻白眼？告诉我。”他说：“嗯，我就是觉得很多人自称设计工程师，但实际上他们并不是。”

turns.en: And I think you can almost caricature it, right? I have this thing with the co-founders where we kind of share out every new job title that comes out. It's not just a design thing, right? You're seeing it in like recruiters who use Claude Code. All of a sudden, they're talent engineers. Okay. There's this post that came out this week from this guy being like, "Oh, there's this new job and it's somebody that helps launch a company out of stealth and they're called a launch engineer." And you're just like, "Okay, where is this gonna stop?" Like, you just—the word engineer means nothing anymore. And that was Oscar's reaction of just like, "Hey, if you're going to describe yourself as a design engineer, then you better be an actual legit designer."
turns.zh: 我觉得这几乎可以漫画化了，对吧？我和联合创始人们有个习惯，就是会分享每一个新出现的职位头衔。这不仅仅是设计领域的事，对吧？你在招聘人员身上也能看到，他们用了 Claude Code，突然之间就成了人才工程师。好吧。这周有个人发了个帖子说：“哦，有个新职位，是帮公司从隐身模式启动的人，他们叫发布工程师。”你就想：“好吧，这什么时候是个头？”就好像“工程师”这个词已经没有任何意义了。Oscar 的反应就是这样：“嘿，如果你要把自己描述成设计工程师，那你最好真的是一个正经的设计师。”

turns.en: That kind of—it's interesting that he has that view because what I've actually started spotting with the people that have all of the skill set to really be like bragging and like having the most inflated job title, they just call themselves product design. Have you noticed this? Like Matt S, he just calls himself a product designer. The guy has over 20 years of experience. He's like one of the most cracked people that I know. He's like super intelligent. Like he's got all the experience—product design.
turns.zh: 那种——有意思的是他有这种观点，因为我实际上开始注意到，那些真正拥有全套技能、完全可以自夸、拥有最夸张头衔的人，他们只叫自己产品设计。你注意到了吗？比如 Matt S，他就只叫自己产品设计师。这家伙有 20 多年的经验。他是我认识的最厉害的人之一。他超级聪明。他拥有所有经验——产品设计。

turns.en: And he's building too. Like he can reach for any combination of engineering.
turns.zh: 而且他也在做开发。他能够触及工程领域的任何组合。

turns.en: I've even seen him say just designer too, and even drop product, which is—I feel like that's maybe where I would land. I'm like, I'm either going to reach for just designer or—don't make fun of me—but like I actually do think there's a window where you could—I can't even say this with a straight face—I think you could say product design engineer, you know, proactively combat some of the buckets that people put you in when you say design engineer. It's like, "No, no, no. I can do product design, but I can also build." I don't know. I think it points at the hilarity of this entire space and time, too.
turns.zh: 我甚至见过他只说设计师，甚至把产品也去掉了，我觉得那可能是我会落脚的地方。我想，我要么就用设计师，要么——别笑话我——但我确实认为有一个窗口，你可以——我都没法板着脸说这个——我觉得你可以说产品设计工程师，你知道，主动对抗一些人们在你自称设计工程师时给你贴的标签。就像：“不不不，我能做产品设计，但我也能开发。”我不知道。我觉得这也指出了整个领域和时代的滑稽之处。

turns.en: I got into a debate with someone recently where I was like—I talked about the product design engineer and they were like, "That doesn't exist. That's not a thing." And I was like, "Why is it not a thing?" And they were like, "Yeah, you know, it's just frustrating to hear when people talk about all these roles merging and then it leads to hiring managers thinking that they only need to hire one person. They don't need to hire all these people anymore." And he was like, "That's not what's happening." I think this is the thing that I can definitely vouch for from all the conversations that I have with hiring managers. A lot of the roles that used to be two to three different people, people are going for one. Whether that's right or whether that's wrong, it's happening, right? And it's also not a new trend. It's not a new trend. People since years ago have talked about the product engineer. This is just an engineer that does product management. Now we've got design engineer. And so I think it's like a natural thing to expect that now that we have these tools at our disposal technically—and I'm not saying that, you know, just hire the one person—you can expect the one person to have way more leverage than before just because they've got access to all these tools that before—I think that that is definitely something even when I look at my own day-to-day things that used to take me days now take me hours, and you know, I think that's happening to everyone.
turns.zh: 我最近和一个人争论过，当时我——我谈到了产品设计工程师，他们说：“那不存在。那不是一回事。”我说：“为什么不是一回事？”他们说：“是啊，你知道，听到人们谈论所有这些角色合并，然后导致招聘经理认为他们只需要雇一个人，这很令人沮丧。他们不再需要雇所有这些不同的人了。”他说：“事实并非如此。”我觉得这是我可以从与招聘经理的所有对话中明确证实的事情。很多过去需要两到三个不同人担任的角色，现在人们只招一个人。无论这是对是错，它正在发生，对吧？而且这也不是新趋势。这不是新趋势。多年前人们就谈论过产品工程师。那只是一个做产品管理的工程师。现在我们有了设计工程师。所以我认为，既然我们在技术上有了这些工具可供使用——我不是说，你知道，只雇一个人——你可以预期这一个人比以前拥有更大的杠杆，因为他们可以使用所有这些工具，以前——我觉得这绝对是事实，即使我看自己日常的事情，过去需要几天的事情现在只需要几个小时，你知道，我认为这发生在每个人身上。

turns.en: And you can do things that you otherwise wouldn't be able to too. We still have the same chart of all of the possible skill sets. I do think that companies are becoming much more interested in drawing circles in more messy middle grounds that kind of overlap different lanes. Another one that I'm seeing a lot is this idea of like a brand engineer. One strain of it is where it's like, you know, we want you to actually come in and build tools, but the tools themselves have to level up the rest of the team with brand and be able to like generate assets or create different visuals. So, you have to be a good brand designer because you have to have the taste to be able to bring all that stuff to life and set the bar for quality. But the output is tools. I think that's an interesting combination I'm seeing. Another one is really blurring the lines between what is a brand designer and what is a web designer. But like if you're a web designer today, you're basically expected to be able to build your designs because everybody can kind of build websites. You know, maybe it really is this idea that like we kind of are tacking on engineer at the end of everything. It just feels so corny to say, but gosh, the expectation, especially in startups and higher profile roles, that you would show up as a builder on top of your existing spikes and skill sets is pretty real. The framing that I've thought about after the conversation with Oscar Lozano—if I described him to someone else as a product designer who is a systems thinker, I think he would be cool with that and I think he would agree with that.
turns.zh: 而且你还能做以前做不到的事情。我们仍然有同样的所有可能技能组合的图表。我确实认为公司越来越感兴趣在更混乱的中间地带画圈，这些地带重叠了不同的轨道。我看到的另一个很多的是品牌工程师这个概念。其中一种类型是，你知道，我们希望你真的进来构建工具，但工具本身必须提升团队其他成员的品牌水平，并且能够生成资产或创建不同的视觉效果。所以，你必须是一个优秀的品牌设计师，因为你必须有品味才能把所有这些变成现实并设定质量标准。但产出是工具。我觉得这是我看到的一个有趣的组合。另一个是真正模糊了品牌设计师和网页设计师之间的界限。但如果你今天是网页设计师，你基本上被期望能够构建你的设计，因为每个人都能构建网站。你知道，也许真的是这个想法，我们好像在一切后面都加上工程师。说起来感觉很老土，但天哪，尤其是在初创公司和更高知名度的职位中，期望你在现有特长和技能组合之上作为一个构建者出现，这是非常真实的。在和 Oscar Lozano 交谈后，我思考的框架是——如果我向别人描述他是一个有系统思维的产品设计师，我想他会接受，而且我认为他会同意。

turns.en: And I think that also applies to the brand engineer that you've just described, which is amazing with brand. Some of the ones that we have in the collective, I wake up in the morning sometimes I'm like wait this person we've put them into like five or six interviews like how are they juggling this? But it's pretty cool right because at that point they know they're in demand. And again, going back to like how I used to think about these things when I was an employee, I'd want the two to three offers at the end because then, you know, you can play the game a little bit and make sure you get the best offer.
turns.zh: 实际上，我不认为设计领域也发生了同样的情况。我这么说是因为我自己经常摆弄 Fable，尝试不同的模型，而到今天我非常确定的一件事是：我能表达出我打开一个产品、摆弄它时想要的感觉，但我没法把它创造出来。我最喜欢的设计师之一——我不知道能不能点名——她在 decimal 的事情上帮了我很多，我去找她，告诉她这就是我想要的感觉，她就能拿出让我有那种感觉的东西。所以我认为正在发生的是，能够把模糊的感觉转化为实际产品的设计师，这些人现在需求大得多。我认为这对招聘经理意味着，旧规则、旧做法、旧招聘方式，你得赶紧摆脱，你得意识到你在为这个人竞争。如果他们优秀，他们很可能会有很多 offer 可选。这么说可能不太公平，但很多情况下，这些人已经有工作了，所以你真的得进来竞争。这意味着给他们更好的体验。这意味着要意识到，是的，他们确实想要这份工作，但如果你想要这个候选人，你就得付出额外努力，并意识到你很可能只是他们最后阶段三个选择之一。所以所有那些旧常态，比如放候选人鸽子、不给他们最好的体验，你可以继续这么做。但别惊讶，如果最后你想要的候选人去了别的地方，因为再说一次，最好的人，最好的人是抢手的。我们 collective 里有些人，我早上醒来有时会想，等等，我们把这个人安排进了五六场面试，他们怎么应付得过来？但这挺酷的，对吧，因为到那时他们知道自己很抢手。再说一次，回到我当员工时怎么想这些事，我会希望在最后拿到两三个 offer，因为那样你可以稍微玩一下游戏，确保自己拿到最好的 offer。

turns.en: So, let's get super specific here. Hypothetically, let's say I'm a hiring manager. I'm one of five companies going after an in-demand designer. What are some best practices, or maybe even hiring pitfalls, that I need to avoid or keep top of mind throughout that process?
turns.zh: 那我们具体一点。假设我是招聘经理，我是五家争抢一位抢手设计师的公司之一。在这个过程中，有哪些最佳实践，或者甚至招聘陷阱，是我需要避免或时刻留意的？

turns.en: One specific hiring manager that comes to mind is Hannah, head of design at Superpower.
turns.zh: 我想到一位具体的招聘经理，是 Superpower 的设计负责人 Hannah。

turns.en: Yeah, she's awesome.
turns.zh: 对，她很棒。

turns.en: One of my favorite hiring managers that we've worked with. She just has this way of, when she sees a portfolio that she likes, the words she uses are just so funny. We shared a portfolio of someone—I actually can't remember who it was—but she said something along the lines of, "I would kill a thousand gorillas to be able to hire this designer." And of course, you made a joke about it. I think you said something along the lines of, "Maybe if you just raise the salary a little bit, you won't need to kill a thousand gorillas."
turns.zh: 她是我们合作过的最喜欢的招聘经理之一。她有一种方式，当她看到一个喜欢的作品集时，她用的词特别搞笑。我们分享了某个人的作品集——我其实不记得是谁了——但她说的大意是：“为了能雇到这个设计师，我愿意杀一千只大猩猩。”当然，你对此开了个玩笑。我记得你说的大意是：“也许你只要把薪水提高一点，就不需要杀一千只大猩猩了。”

turns.en: As a result of her saying that, of course, the natural thing that I do is I want to screenshot that and send that to the candidate. I've never been a recruiter before. I don't know whether that was unprofessional of me to do. I mean, whatever. I did it anyway. And the candidate was like, "Oh my god, I want to frame this. This is so cool. I feel so special." And it's almost like that is the theme, right? If you realize that these designers are in demand, how do you make them feel special? Doing the small things, like sending them a personalized note. We ended up building a whole feature for hiring managers to be able to send a personalized note on Decimals. And pretty recently, we've even had someone go a step further, which is like, "Hey, I want to send candidates a personalized video where I'm going to spend 3 minutes and go through their portfolio. I'm going to tell them why I think their portfolio is excellent, and then I'm going to do the pitch to them." And all of this is before they have even had—oh yeah, I'm interested. They're realizing that they need to pitch this designer in order to get that first interview.
turns.zh: 因为她说了那句话，当然，我自然而然就想截图发给候选人。我以前从没做过招聘。我不知道那样做是否不专业。反正，我还是做了。候选人的反应是：“天哪，我想把它裱起来。这太酷了。我觉得自己很特别。”这几乎就是主题，对吧？如果你意识到这些设计师很抢手，你怎么让他们感到特别？做一些小事，比如发一条个性化的留言。我们最终为招聘经理在 Decimals 上建了一个完整的功能，让他们能发个性化留言。最近甚至有人更进一步，说：“嘿，我想给候选人发一段个性化视频，我会花 3 分钟浏览他们的作品集，告诉他们为什么我觉得他们的作品集很棒，然后向他们做推介。”而这一切都发生在他们还没——哦对，我感兴趣——之前。他们意识到，为了得到第一次面试，他们需要向这位设计师做推介。

turns.en: Something I've noticed is that all the new startups that are fresh off a seed round, they all think they are the single coolest company in the entire world. And everybody just assumes that every designer is going to drop everything and want to get in line to work for them. And that is just not the case. If you are targeting this persona that knows they're in demand, you almost have to put a little bit of a sales hat on, right? It's half sales, half interviewing. In the same way that, going back to what you talked about earlier with Claire, in every conversation she's having, she's 50% presenting herself and 50% interviewing that company to see if they're even worth her strongly considering. I would almost flip it and talk about the Doug Dues.
turns.zh: 我注意到，所有刚完成种子轮融资的新创公司，都觉得自己是全世界最酷的公司。每个人都假设每个设计师都会放下一切，排队想为他们工作。但事实并非如此。如果你瞄准的是这种知道自己很抢手的人，你几乎得戴上一点销售的帽子，对吧？一半是销售，一半是面试。就像你之前提到 Claire 时说的，在她进行的每一次对话中，她 50% 是在展示自己，50% 是在面试那家公司，看他们是否值得她认真考虑。我几乎想反过来，谈谈 Doug Dues。

turns.en: And I think we see these quite often, right? To your point, somebody that's just raised a seed round and they're really excited about their product, but then they turn up and they've never had a designer work on their product, and you open up the website and you can tell, right? Again, I feel comfortable saying this. I'm not a designer. I would definitely have fallen into this camp before starting Just—like, "Ah, it looks good enough." A designer looks at that and they're like, "This person clearly doesn't care about design. No, I'm not going to take the interview. I don't want to speak to this person." I think that's one of the basic ones. I think really, really long processes is another one. Having the eight, nine rounds. Again, I feel like that's something that belongs to the old world. I went through that. As somebody that went through it and successfully got the job a couple of times, there is nothing valuable that you get from giving me 8 or 45-minute interviews with different people that are all asking me different variations of the same question.
turns.zh: 我想我们经常看到这种情况，对吧？就像你说的，有人刚完成种子轮融资，对自己的产品非常兴奋，但然后他们出现了，却从没有设计师参与过他们的产品，你打开网站就能看出来，对吧？再说一次，我说这话很自在。我不是设计师。在创办 Just 之前，我肯定会落入这个阵营——就像，“啊，看起来够好了。”设计师看到后会想：“这个人显然不在乎设计。不，我不会接受面试。我不想和这个人说话。”我认为这是基本的一条。我认为非常非常长的流程是另一条。有八、九轮面试。再说一次，我觉得那属于旧世界。我经历过。作为一个经历过并成功几次拿到工作的人，让我参加 8 场 45 分钟的面试，不同的人都在问我同一个问题的不同变体，你从中得不到任何有价值的东西。

turns.en: Just get to a work. Just let's work together. Let's work through a problem together. That's gonna give you way more information than me being able to come up with variations of the answer of like, "Tell me about a time when blah blah blah." It's like, come on, that can be gamed.
turns.zh: 直接进入工作。就让我们一起工作。让我们一起解决一个问题。那会给你比我能够编造出“告诉我一次你 blah blah blah”的答案变体多得多的信息。就像，拜托，那可以被钻空子。

turns.en: I talked to a friend recently on that note who almost everybody listening to this would know, and they've been working at a very high-profile company. They had their pick of the litter, and he didn't even respond to companies that didn't lead with him in his first touch point being able to talk to somebody on the executive team or like the head of design. If you presented a first step and said, "Yeah, you know, speak to our recruiter," he didn't even respond. He's out. And yeah, I get it—not everybody's in that position, but if you want to play at that tier, it's the only way to do it.
turns.zh: 说到这个，我最近和一位朋友聊过，几乎每个听这个节目的人都会认识他，他一直在一家非常高调的公司工作。他有很多选择，他甚至不回复那些第一次接触不是让他和高管团队或设计负责人交谈的公司。如果你提出的第一步是说：“对，你知道，和我们的招聘人员谈谈，”他根本不会回复。他就出局了。是的，我明白——不是每个人都处于那个位置，但如果你想在那个层级玩，这是唯一的办法。

turns.en: In the same way that I said you don't get a second chance to create a first impression on the designer side, I think that's also true for the hiring manager side, right? And an example of somebody who does this very well is Matt Herzog at LiveKit, where his first round is like, "Talk to me first. Let's have a chat one-on-one, you and me." It's actually pretty different to how most companies do it. Most companies do the recruiter screen first, but I just don't think that's the right way of doing it, because you are putting somebody who is not a designer and you're getting them to do a screen for a design job. That doesn't make any sense at all to me. The way that makes sense is what Matt at LiveKit has done, which is like, "Let me do the first bit. If we have a good chat and I get a good feeling, I pass you on to the recruiter and they can do the screen and talk through the logistics, location, salary, all that kind of stuff." There's still a place for that, but just don't make it the first thing.
turns.zh: 就像我说过的，在设计师这边，你没有第二次机会来创造第一印象，我认为招聘经理这边也是如此，对吧？一个做得非常好的例子是 LiveKit 的 Matt Herzog，他的第一轮是：“先和我谈。我们一对一聊聊，你和我。”这实际上和大多数公司的做法很不同。大多数公司先做招聘人员筛选，但我就是不认为那是正确的做法，因为你让一个不是设计师的人来做设计工作的筛选。这对我来说完全说不通。说得通的做法是 LiveKit 的 Matt 所做的，就像：“让我来做第一部分。如果我们聊得好，我感觉不错，我就把你转给招聘人员，他们可以做筛选，谈谈后勤、地点、薪水之类的。”那仍然有它的位置，但别把它放在第一位。

turns.en: I get a lot of questions from startups asking about how to structure the hiring process. We've talked about condensing broadly, maybe leading with a first touch point that isn't a recruiter. Another sub-question in that topic—I have a ton of DMs and I'm basically just going to outsource my answer to you—is around this idea of: do we do a take-home assignment? Does that take-home assignment need to be paid? Should it be about the product? Should we skip that and do a work trial? What are you kind of noticing? And do you have any recommendations for, again, that startup that maybe just raised a seed round that's looking for that founding designer?
turns.zh: 我收到很多来自初创公司的问题，问如何构建招聘流程。我们大致谈过压缩流程，也许以不是招聘人员的第一次接触开始。这个话题下的另一个子问题——我收到一大堆私信，我基本上就把我的回答外包给你了——是关于这个想法：我们要不要做带回家的作业？那个带回家的作业需要付费吗？它应该关于产品吗？我们应该跳过那个，做工作试用吗？你注意到什么？对于那家可能刚完成种子轮融资、正在寻找创始设计师的初创公司，你有什么建议吗？

turns.en: There's two companies that come to mind that I think do it particularly well.
turns.zh: 我想到两家公司，我认为他们做得特别好。

turns.en: One of those is Lovable Nad you've obviously had on the podcast a bunch of times and like is such a thoughtful and really really smart guy and Hannah from Superpower. and they both have pretty similar approaches which is for them the work trial part is really important and Hannah even goes to the extreme of let's do a vibe check at the beginning and then let's just get straight into the work and that to me is so refreshing again because I think anything else about the interview about the behavioral questions about there's whole books written about how you can like prepare for these interviews and my whole thing is like it just it feels like theatrics It feels like if I have to think about five examples of things that I've done in my career and tell you about how amazing I was and and create the arc and tell you about the problem and that it's like what is the point? You're not hiring me to be a politician. You're not hiring me to be a spokesperson. You are hiring a designer. And so just get into the design work. Like stop stop trying to create an overly complex process for something that is pretty simple. And I think that's how Hannah approaches it, which is like if the vibe is good and you know some basics are checked, let's get straight into the work trial. And I think that's just so especially in today's day and age where so much is being spoken about, things that are being faked, things that are being cheated on. It's just like let's get straight into a work crow especially if they're in the same office. And of course there are like things to keep in mind. Make sure that it's paid. make sure that you don't focus too much on the outcome and the artifact, more on the like back and forth. And I think one of the ways that I look at it personally is like if I'm hiring a designer, I want to see how they react the first time that I tell them that I I disagree with something or that I I would like to take a different perspective because that's the human thing, right? That's the thing that if we're going to work together, the great times are great, but there's going to be times where there's going to be friction and that's a healthy thing. You should work through that.
turns.zh: 其中一个就是 Lovable Nad，你显然已经多次邀请他上播客了，他是个非常有思想、非常非常聪明的人，还有 Superpower 的 Hannah。他们的方法非常相似，对他们来说，工作试用部分非常重要，Hannah 甚至极端到一开始先做个氛围检查，然后直接进入工作。这对我来说太令人耳目一新了，因为我认为任何其他关于面试、行为问题、有整本书教你如何准备这些面试的东西，我的整个想法是，这感觉像演戏。感觉就像如果我必须想出五个我职业生涯中的例子，告诉你我有多棒，并构建一个故事弧，告诉你问题是什么，那有什么意义？你雇我不是让我当政客。你雇我不是让我当发言人。你雇的是设计师。所以直接进入设计工作吧。别为一件相当简单的事情创造一个过于复杂的流程。我认为 Hannah 就是这样做的，如果氛围好，而且你知道一些基本条件都满足了，就直接进入工作试用。我认为这尤其适用于当今这个时代，有太多关于造假、作弊的讨论。就像直接进入工作试用吧，尤其是如果他们在同一个办公室。当然，有一些事情要注意。确保它是带薪的。确保你不要太关注结果和产出物，而更关注来回互动。我个人看待这件事的方式之一是，如果我要雇一个设计师，我想看看当我第一次告诉他们我不同意某事或我想换个角度时，他们如何反应，因为这是人性，对吧？如果我们一起工作，美好的时光很美好，但也会有摩擦的时候，这是健康的。你应该通过它来工作。

turns.en: Okay, so we've talked about all of the things that are shifting in today's hiring landscape. What about comp? What are we seeing there? Can you give people who are maybe either in the market or considering what might be next a little window into state of the world for compensation?
turns.zh: 好了，我们已经讨论了当今招聘格局中所有正在变化的事情。那薪酬呢？我们在那里看到了什么？你能给那些可能在市场上或考虑下一步的人一个小窗口，了解薪酬的现状吗？

turns.en: I think a theme that I feel pretty confident standing behind is that the fact that one person has way more leverage than ever before does mean that a team can say, "Right, we're going to hire less people, but the people that we hire, we're going to give them better salaries." We're in a little bubble, right? Most of the companies that we work with, it's like SF New York. There's clearly a lot of competition there. But whenever I speak to somebody who either doesn't know that market well and they find out some of the salaries of the like design engineers or I don't I mean we're going to talk about salaries so I'm not going to talk about individuals but some of the recent ones that we've placed into like design engineer roles or like pretty senior product design roles they're making 300 grand or close to that I think to a lot of people would be like oh wow I would have expected that to be like engineering salaries but I think that is the general theme of like if If you're in demand, supply and demand, like if there's not enough supply, then you're going to need to pay and compete more. So, I think that is definitely like a a theme that I see playing out. And then the other thing that I think I've seen playing out is some of these folks are starting to realize, and I think where I've seen it most acutely is in brand roles. brand right now is so hard to hire for because there's this complete mismatch of the company side who think that a brand designer they can pay less than a product designer or than a design engineer and then you have the other side of the like the person who they might call themselves a brand engineer but you know they're a brand designer with systems thinking
turns.zh: 我认为一个我很有信心支持的主题是，一个人比以往任何时候都拥有更大的杠杆，这确实意味着团队可以说：“对，我们要少雇人，但我们雇的人，我们要给他们更好的薪水。”我们处在一个小泡沫里，对吧？我们合作的大多数公司，都在旧金山、纽约。那里显然有很多竞争。但每当我与那些不太了解那个市场的人交谈，他们发现一些设计工程师的薪水时，或者——我的意思是，我们要谈薪水，所以我不会谈具体个人，但最近我们安置到设计工程师职位或相当资深的产品设计职位的一些人，他们赚 30 万或接近这个数。我认为对很多人来说会想，哦哇，我本以为那是工程薪水。但我认为这就是一般主题，如果你有需求，供需关系，如果供应不足，你就需要支付更多并竞争。所以，我认为这绝对是我看到的一个主题。然后我看到的另一件事是，这些人开始意识到，我认为我最敏锐地看到这一点是在品牌角色中。品牌现在很难招聘，因为公司方面认为品牌设计师可以比产品设计师或设计工程师付得少，而另一方面，有些人可能自称品牌工程师，但你知道他们是具有系统思维的品牌设计师。

turns.en: Sure
turns.zh: 当然

turns.en: and they're realizing that actually if I can build you the system and I don't need to be a full-time employee and the system allows you to self-s serve for a lot of the stuff that you usually need a full-time time hire for then guess what you don't need to hire me full-time maybe you hire me as a freelancer maybe you hire me as a contractor and people realizing that they can freelance and charge pretty hefty amounts I don't know whether we want to name name him but there's a a brand designer that we both know who literally told me was like hey I'm freelancing I make 500 to 750k a year and that's going to be outrageous to most founders but if you want to talk to me about a full-time role that's my baseline and of course for most people that would be like no we don't have that's like probably four or five people's salaries. So so you see that mismatch a little bit.
turns.zh: 他们意识到，实际上如果我能为你构建系统，我不需要是全职员工，系统允许你自助服务很多通常需要全职雇佣的事情，那么猜猜怎么着，你不需要全职雇我，也许你雇我作为自由职业者，也许你雇我作为承包商。人们意识到他们可以自由职业并收取相当高的费用。我不知道我们是否想点名，但我们都认识的一位品牌设计师，他直接告诉我：“嘿，我自由职业，我一年赚 50 到 75 万。”这对大多数创始人来说会是离谱的，但如果你想和我谈全职角色，那就是我的底线。当然，对大多数人来说，那会像是“不，我们没有那个”，那大概是四五个人的薪水。所以你看到了一点这种不匹配。

turns.en: Well it's encouraging that yeah maybe we're being asked to do a little bit more as designers but we do have more leverage in terms of comp. Before I let you go I do want to hear just a little bit more about your journey because I find it particularly inspiring and I I always just I want more people to start companies. I I want more people to go out and start their own thing, try it, build things. And you're a great example of what that kind of looks like. And so maybe just give us a little bit of the background like what has it been like going on your own founder journey? Anything that's surprising or even just the assumptions that maybe you made about the the hiring market or what this shape of business would look like?
turns.zh: 嗯，这很令人鼓舞，是的，也许作为设计师我们被要求做更多一点，但我们在薪酬方面确实有更多杠杆。在我让你走之前，我确实想多听一点你的旅程，因为我觉得它特别鼓舞人心，我总是希望更多人创办公司。我希望更多人出去开始自己的事情，尝试它，构建东西。你是一个很好的例子，展示了那看起来像什么。所以也许给我们一点背景，比如你自己的创始人旅程是什么样的？有什么令人惊讶的，或者甚至是你对招聘市场或这种业务形态所做的假设？

turns.en: I think it's the most fascinating time to be a founder right now just because there's so much that's changing. If we rewind to like 12 or it was about a year ago that we started Decimals, I had no background as a recruiter, no background as a designer. This was a completely new world to me if anything because of that because I had no like best practices or you know norms to like be attached to. I think a pretty contrarian view that we had early on was that like if we manage to create an experience that candidates really love, we'll be able to get the best candidates and hence the companies will follow. And I think that's pretty contrarian relative to a lot of founders in this space that are like they see where the where where the money is coming from and who's paying them and they think right we just need to focus on that. And so like one thing that I I think about a lot is there's a lot of kind of founders going into the space purely seeing this as an algorithmic problem of like hey we need to create the perfect algorithm that finds a match between a resume and a job description.
turns.zh: 我认为现在是成为创始人最迷人的时候，因为变化太多了。如果我们回溯到大约 12 个月前，或者大约一年前我们创办 Decimals 时，我没有招聘背景，没有设计背景。这对我来说是一个全新的世界，如果有的话，正因为如此，因为我没有最佳实践或规范可以依附。我认为我们早期有一个相当反传统的观点，那就是如果我们设法创造一种候选人真正喜欢的体验，我们就能得到最好的候选人，因此公司会跟随。我认为这相对于这个领域的许多创始人来说是相当反传统的，他们看到钱从哪里来，谁付钱给他们，他们认为对，我们只需要专注于那个。所以我经常思考的一件事是，有很多创始人进入这个领域，纯粹将其视为一个算法问题，比如嘿，我们需要创建完美的算法，在简历和工作描述之间找到匹配。

transcript.sec: What I Learned in a Year

turns.en: A year into this, what I have actually realized is that those two artifacts are really, really not worth the paper that they've written on. We see it time and time again. A hiring manager comes in and they say this is the maximum salary we're ever going to pay, we're never going to pay more than this, and the candidate needs to be in this location, and it needs to be a full five days in office role. And then the dream designer comes along, and all of those rules go out the window. And all of a sudden they're like, oh no, look, for this candidate, yeah, okay, we'll raise the salary. Oh, you want to work remote? Oh yeah, let's work, let's make it work. And so that's been one of the really surprising things for me, again, coming into this as somebody without the background, of just realizing what people say and what they do are very different things. Because of that, I think we've just taken a slightly different approach to how we've built Decimals and so like the thinking. And so it's very much a beginner's mindset and just trying to create an experience that we'd be happy to go through as candidates ourselves. A year in, and I've basically learned that I don't know anything and that I've still got so much to learn.
turns.zh: 一年下来，我真正意识到的是，那两份文件真的真的不值它们写在上面的那张纸。我们一次又一次地看到这种情况。招聘经理进来说，这是我们能给的最高薪资，我们绝不会付得比这更多，而且候选人必须在这个地点，必须是全职、每周五天到办公室。然后那个梦寐以求的设计师出现了，所有这些规则就全被抛到窗外了。突然之间他们就说，哦不，你看，对这个候选人，好吧，我们加薪。哦，你想远程工作？哦对，我们想办法，我们让它行得通。所以这对我来说是真正令人惊讶的事情之一，再次强调，作为一个没有背景的人进入这个领域，就是意识到人们说的和做的完全是两回事。正因为如此，我想我们在构建 Decimals 的方式上采取了一种稍微不同的方法，就是这种思路。所以这非常像一种初学者心态，只是试图创造一种我们自己作为候选人会乐意经历的体验。一年下来，我基本上学到的是我什么都不懂，而且我还有太多东西要学。

turns.en: Beginner's mindset is probably the most important mindset for anybody doing anything nowadays, just with the rate of change. So, I appreciate you, Danny. I appreciate everything that you shared today and your willingness to come on and kind of pull back the curtain and show like what's actually happening in today's market. And also just the fact that you're investing in this model and way of supporting designers. Like, it's so incredibly designer friendly in a way that gets me excited and is something that I wanted to continue to be a part of. So, I appreciate you and uh I'm excited to get this set of insights out into the world.
turns.zh: 初学者心态可能是如今任何人做任何事最重要的心态，就因为变化的速度。所以，我感谢你，Danny。我感谢你今天分享的一切，也感谢你愿意来，揭开帷幕，展示当今市场实际发生的情况。还有你投资于这种模式和支持设计师的方式。它以一种让我兴奋的方式对设计师极其友好，也是我想继续参与其中的事情。所以，我感谢你，呃，我很兴奋能把这一系列见解分享给世界。

turns.en: All right, man. Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 好的，伙计。谢谢你邀请我。
